{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"On the first day of autumn, Mateo found a tiny greenhouse behind the town library. Its glass panes were cloudy, and ivy curled around the door, but inside, rows of empty pots waited beneath a roof of green-tinted light.

A woman in a red scarf was sweeping fallen leaves from the path.

“Is this garden yours?” Mateo asked.

“It belongs to anyone willing to care for it,” she replied. Her name was Mrs. Lin, and she had tended the greenhouse for many years. Lately, though, her hands had grown stiff, and she could no longer manage the plants alone.

Mateo offered to help. Each Wednesday after school, he watered the seedlings, loosened the soil, and swept the narrow paths. Mrs. Lin taught him how to recognize thirsty leaves and how to move young plants without hurting their roots.

As winter approached, the greenhouse grew warm and bright against the cold. Mateo planted tiny lettuce seeds and labeled each pot with a wooden marker. He also placed a small bench near the entrance so visitors could sit and watch the rain bead on the glass.

One afternoon, a little girl came in with her father. She had never seen anything growing indoors and stared in wonder at the green shoots.

“Could I plant something too?” she asked.

Mrs. Lin handed her a pot and a packet of seeds. Soon, other visitors began stopping by. Some brought empty containers; others offered stories about gardens they remembered.

By spring, the greenhouse was full of herbs, flowers, and vegetables. Mateo looked around at the crowded shelves and smiled.

Mrs. Lin rested beside the doorway, listening to the lively hum of visitors.

“A garden grows best when it is shared,” she said.

Mateo understood. The greenhouse had become more than a place for plants. It had become a place where people put down roots together."}
